original_question: Let X1 and X2 be Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, and suppose there is an equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) that commutes with the degree shift functors of X1 and X2. What additional assumptions on Phi are sufficient to conclude that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target extremely closely. It has the right geometric objects (Gushel–Mukai fourfolds), the right categorical invariant (the Kuznetsov component Ku(X)), the key compatibility hypothesis singled out in the paper (commuting with the degree shift functors), and the right conclusion being sought (isomorphism of the fourfolds rather than merely birationality or equality of period points).

refined_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth complex Gushel–Mukai fourfolds, and let Ku(X_i):=⟨O_{X_i}, U_{X_i}^∨, O_{X_i}(1), U_{X_i}^∨(1)⟩^⊥ ⊂ D^b(X_i) be their Kuznetsov components. Assume there is an exact equivalence Φ: Ku(X1) →~ Ku(X2) together with a natural isomorphism Φ∘𝖮_{X_1} ≅ 𝖮_{X_2}∘Φ, where the degree shift functor is 𝖮_{X_i}:=L_{⟨O_{X_i},U_{X_i}^∨⟩}(-⊗O_{X_i}(1))[-1]. Under what additional assumptions on Φ is one allowed to conclude that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s official open problem. In Section 7.3, after explaining that ordinary Torelli fails for GM fourfolds and that equivalence of Kuznetsov components alone does not recover the period point, the authors isolate degree-shift compatibility as the extra structure to impose and then formulate exactly this open question as Question 7.16. Remark 7.17 gives the nearest sharper neighboring statement: an intermediate problem asking whether such a Φ induces a Hodge isometry on H^4_van, and it explains that this intermediate implication is known. So the faithful refinement is to keep Question 7.16 itself, but make its notation and functorial hypotheses fully explicit.
